children: Nestle (NSRGY), the global food-and-beverage producer, lost control of its Russian operations after a presidential decree placed the business under temporary external administration. The shares shown in the chart were priced at $92.82 on September 18. Reuters reported that Nestle fell about 1.3% in European trading as investors reacted to the move.

The Russian operation is still substantial on the ground, with six factories and roughly 7,000 employees. Nestle said it is assessing its options and intends to take the steps necessary to protect its rights and maintain business continuity, particularly for employees. Russia accounted for about $2.4 billion of Nestle sales in 2021, but the company has since sharply reduced its presence and limited investment and product availability.

The chart adds an important valuation angle. At $92.82, Nestle trades 9.31% below its GF Value of $102.35, suggesting the market price already carries a meaningful discount to GuruFocus' estimate of fair value. That does not remove the Russia risk: temporary administration can still translate into an impairment, a forced exit or a prolonged loss of economic control. But with Russia now representing a much smaller piece of the group than it once did, the bigger investor question is whether the balance-sheet hit ultimately proves larger than the underlying earnings exposure.

title: Nestle Slides 1.3% as Russia Takes Temporary Control
